headline: Join the Royal Navy in 2026: Requirements, Fitness and Application Guide
metaDescription: Royal Navy recruitment 2026: age 16-42, 2.4km PJFT run times, BMI and swimming standards, DAA aptitude test, Commonwealth rules and HMS Raleigh training.

sections.content:
The Royal Navy recruits ratings and officers into warfare, engineering, logistics, medical and aviation branches. General Entry ratings need no formal qualifications, while officer candidates need at least 72 UCAS points plus five GCSEs at grades 9-4 including English and mathematics. Age limits run 16 to 42 for ratings and 18 to 42 for officers.

Applicants must be British or Irish nationals, Commonwealth citizens or eligible dual nationals, with body mass index between 18 and 28. Every applicant passes the Naval Swimming Test, because life at sea demands water confidence from day one of training.
sections.title: Roles, Age and Nationality Requirements

sections.content:
The Pre-Joining Fitness Test is a 2.4km run with times set by age and gender. Men aged 16 to 24 must finish in 13 minutes 56 seconds, rising to 16 minutes 3 seconds at 40 to 44; women aged 16 to 24 get 16 minutes 27 seconds. Candidates attending the careers office before 1 October 2026 take this run version.

Beyond the run, recruits face medical screening for vision, hearing and general health, plus a full fitness assessment during the first weeks of Phase 1 training. Arriving already able to pass makes the transition to service life far easier.
sections.title: Fitness, BMI and Medical Standards

sections.content:
The application starts with registering interest on the Royal Navy careers site. Candidates then complete the Defence Aptitude Assessment, a computer-based test of maths, English and reasoning, followed by a formal selection interview about motivation and suitability.

Medical examinations and security vetting follow, with background checks often the longest stage. Officers additionally face the Admiralty Interview Board, which assesses leadership, intellect and character over several days before entry is confirmed.
sections.title: Selection: DAA, Interview and Vetting

sections.content:
Successful recruits begin Phase 1 training at HMS Raleigh in Cornwall, learning drill, seamanship, weapons handling and naval ethos before specialist training in their branch. Officers train at Britannia Royal Naval College in Dartmouth.

Pay starts on a published scale with free medical and dental care, subsidised accommodation and a non-contributory pension. The Navy also offers funded qualifications, adventurous training and clear progression from able rate through senior ratings, or from midshipman to commissioned ranks.
